task: SHELFCHECK — DOSSIER CONTAMINATION REPAIR — FINAL BATCH
selection: The final 14 entries in manifest array order, following the 70 handled by Batches 1-4 (PR #40, #41, #42, #43). This closes the original 84-entry manifest completely.
method: For each of the 14 titles, loaded the base shelfcheck-dossiers.txt entry and replayed every existing dossier-overrides-*.js batch (1 through 48, in real load order) using the same last-write-wins Map.set logic dossier-apply.js uses at runtime, to determine the actual EFFECTIVE (live) dossier object -- not just whether an override file happens to mention the title. An entry was classified ALREADY_FIXED only when the effective object was a distinct, already-accurate override (verified against the real game); LIVE_CONTAMINATED (-> REPAIRED) when the effective object was still the contaminated base entry itself.

finalManifestReconciliation.method: Programmatically parsed the ids and classifications recorded in all five repair-batch audit artifacts (batch 1's 'repairs' array, using its 'correction' text starting with 'No change made' as the ALREADY_FIXED signal, and batches 2-5's 'classifications' arrays) and compared the combined id list against the original 84-id dossierContaminationFullManifest from audit-out/curation-verification-pass-1.json. Confirmed: exact set equality (every manifest id appears exactly once across the five batches, no id appears in more than one batch, no inspected id is absent from the original manifest), yielding a perfect 84-of-84 1:1 match with zero duplicates and zero gaps.

notesForReviewer: This is the final batch: all 84 entries from the original contamination manifest are now accounted for exactly once, across batches 1-5 (PR #40, #41, #42, #43, and this PR).

3 of these final 14 were classified ALREADY_FIXED (Super Cane Magic ZERO, SuperMash, Surf World Series), all with their effective override already living in dossier-overrides-45.js -- each already supersedes the contaminated base shelfcheck-dossiers.txt entry at runtime, so Josh has never seen the wrong text for any of these 3. Each was independently re-verified against the real game and deliberately left untouched.

11 of these final 14 were classified REPAIRED (genuinely LIVE_CONTAMINATED): no override existed, so the contaminated base text was what ShelfCheck actually served. New, game-specific overrides for these 11 were added in a new file, dossier-overrides-49.js, following the exact same {t,s,w,c,r,b,p} object-literal schema as every prior batch.

WordHunters's dossier text is now accurate about the actual game while explicitly noting it remains excluded from the Josh Set (LOW_VALUE_ACTIVITY, curation pass #1) -- this repair only touched dossier content, not census status.

World Poker Championship required disambiguation research: its base contamination (a Coresoft company bio) is entirely unrelated, since Coresoft's own poker series never released on PS4. This specific ShelfCheck identity is a distinct, separately-published (Play It) budget poker title, explicitly distinguished in the new dossier from the similarly-named 'Pure Hold'em World Poker Championship' by Ripstone/VooFoo Studios to avoid conflating the two.

Zombie Vikings's curator take draws an evidence-supported connection to the Josh-confirmed hit Stick it to the Man! (same studio Zoink, same hand-drawn art style and humor per multiple reviews) while being explicit that this specific personal-fit claim is a prediction, not a claim that Josh has played this title.

dossier-apply.js, index.html, and sw.js each received exactly one minimal line-edit to register/precache the new batch file, consistent with every prior batch; sw.js's cache generation was bumped shelfcheck-v138 -> shelfcheck-v139.
